title: Platform systems & services — dashboards, runbooks, roadmap, and team wiki
author: Jordan Mitchell
content:
Overview
========
This document is the canonical platform engineering reference for systems and services owned by the Platform team. It combines a systems inventory, dashboard catalog, alerting and runbooks, quarterly retrospective findings, and a forward-looking roadmap. Use this page when onboarding, triaging incidents, or planning platform work.

Scope
-----
- All central platform services (control-plane APIs, routing, model-proxy, batching layer, KV-caching, telemetry ingestion)
- Dashboards and alerting that surface customer-impacting SLOs and platform health
- Oncall runbooks and escalation paths for Severity 1/2 incidents
- Team wiki ownership and roadmap milestones for the next three quarters

1. Systems & Services inventory
------------------------------
Below are the primary services with owners, critical SLOs, and current operational notes. If you add a new service, update this table and create a platform component dashboard (see section 2).

| Service | Owner | Critical SLOs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| control-plane-api | Platform API Team (owner: Priya Rao) | 99.95% availability, p95 latency < 120ms | Handles auth, routing, model selection. Degraded when db-metadata lag > 10s. |
| model-proxy | Serving Runtime (owner: Marco Nguyen) | 99.9% availability for model routing; error rate < 0.5% | Auto-fallback to smaller model variants on OOM. |
| batching-layer | Serving Runtime (owner: Maria Gomez) | Throughput SLO: maintain 95% of reserved throughput; median batching delay < 15ms | Backpressure to callers when queue > 80% capacity. |
| kv-cache | Cache Team (owner: Samir Patel) | Cache hit-rate > 70% for popular prefixes | Warm-up scripts in repo infra/caching. |
| telemetry-ingest | Observability (owner: Zoe Kim) | Ingest latency < 30s; no dropped spans > 0.1% | Uses kafka -> flusher pattern; monitor lags. |

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owners listed above. Pager rotations for Platform and Serving Runtime teams are in the Team Wiki.
- For cross-team incidents, open a cross-functional incident channel (#inc-<id>-platform) and notify the oncall leads for Product and Security.

2. Dashboards catalog (what to check first)
-----------------------------------------
Key dashboards (links are internal to the Team Wiki):
- Platform Overview Dashboard — SRE > Platform > Overview (shows combined availability, request QPS, total tokens/sec)
- Control Plane Health — Platform > Control-plane (auth failures, DB metadata lag, p95 latencies)
- Serving Runtime Ops — Serving Runtime > Model-proxy (model load failures, OOMs, GPU utilization)
- Batching and Queueing — Serving Runtime > Batching-layer (queue depth, batching delay histogram)
- Cost & Capacity — Platform > Capacity (reserved vs consumed GPU hours, surge buffer)
- Telemetry & Logs Ingest — Observability > Ingest (kafka lag, dropped spans)

Dashboard best practices
- Primary SLOs on top-left; critical alerts next to SLOs.
- Use cohort filters: environment=prod, region=us-west-2, tenant=all
- Add one-line notes for known instrumentation caveats (e.g., p50 measurement excludes cold-starts).

3. Alerts, thresholds and intent
--------------------------------
These are the platform-alerting intents that map to runbooks and severity levels. Maintain alerts as short-lived rules with clear runbook links.

Alert matrix (examples):
- control-plane-api-auth-failure-rate (Severity 2) — trigger when 10m error rate > 1% and sustained for 10m. Intent: investigate DB metadata + auth provider. Pager: control-plane oncall. Runbook: section 4.
- model-proxy-ooms (Severity 1) — trigger when OOMs > 5 across any model shard in 5m. Intent: immediate fallback to smaller model, scale up or drain nodes. Pager: serving-runtime oncall + platform lead. Runbook: section 4.
- batching-queue-depth-high (Severity 2) — queue depth > 80% of capacity for 5m. Intent: inspect downstream throughput, increase worker pool or reduce per-request token budgets. Pager: serving-runtime oncall.
- telemetry-kafka-lag (Severity 2) — consumer lag > 300k messages for 10m. Intent: restart flusher, add consumer instances. Pager: observability oncall.

Alert contents should include
- Why this matters (customer impact)
- Quick triage checklist (4–6 steps)
- Remediation actions and safe rollbacks
- Owners & escalation path
- Link to runbook and recent postmortems

4. Runbooks — Severity 1 and Severity 2 (example playbooks)
----------------------------------------------------------
General rules before any action:
- If the incident is customer impacting (affects API availability or correctness) mark Severity 1 and notify CS and Product.
- Annotate the incident timeline in the incident doc (use incident-template.md).
- If unsure about scope, assume wider blast radius and escalate to Platform Lead.

Runbook: model-proxy-ooms (Severity 1)
1) Detect & confirm: check Serving Runtime Ops dashboard for OOM spikes, list of affected shards.
2) Contain: enable automated fallback: set traffic to fallback_model:<smaller-variant> in the router (CLI: infra router set-fallback --model model-xyz --variant quant-8bit-small).
3) Stabilize: scale up pod group: kubectl -n serving scale deployment/model-proxy --replicas=+3 (follow capacity plan to ensure you do not exceed reserved GPU quota).
4) Mitigate latency impacts: temporarily lower batching target to reduce memory pressure: POST /admin/batching-config {"target_tokens": 128}.
5) Post-incident: collect heap dumps and kernel logs, open PR with RCA notes and recommended config change.

Runbook: control-plane-auth-failure-rate (Severity 2)
1) Confirm error source: query auth-proxy logs and control-plane-api metrics.
2) Check DB metadata replication lag (db-meta-lag > 10s indicates root cause).
3) If auth provider is down, toggle maintenance mode and serve cached tokens (CLI: controlplane maintenance enable --reason "ext-auth-failure").
4) If DB issues, fail open to read-only metadata and rollback recent schema migration.
5) Post-incident: schedule migration postmortem and change the runbook if recovered via manual steps.

5. How-tos (recipes)
--------------------
A. Adding a new dashboard
1. Create dashboard in Grafana with the component prefix: team:platform:<service-name>
2. Top-left: SLO panel (explicit SLOs), Top-right: Error rate panel, below: latency and resource panels
3. Add annotations for deploys and incidents (Grafana annotations)
4. Link dashboard id into this page and the service README

B. Creating or tuning an alert
1. Document the intent and customer impact in the alert description.
2. Use a 30m evaluation window for noisy signals and require 2 consecutive evaluation periods for firing.
3. Add a runbook link and oncall rotation contact.
4. Test the alert in staging and verify runbook steps before promoting to prod.

C. Onboarding new Platform service
1. Add a row to the Systems Inventory table above.
2. Create a dashboard and alert set per templates in /ops/templates.
3. Add SLOs and link to the SLA page in product-docs.
4. Request a security review (see security-and-compliance checklist).

6. Retrospective: Q2 2026 highlights and action items
---------------------------------------------------
Summary: We saw three Severity 1 incidents in Q2: one model-proxy OOM cascade, one telemetry ingestion lag, and one control-plane DB migration fallout. Root causes were a combination of config drift, insufficient canary coverage for DB migrations, and an untested fallback path for a new quantized model.

Key action items (owner, due)
- Strengthen pre-merge canary tests for DB migrations (owner: infra-db, due: 2026-08-31)
- Add automated canary traffic for new model variants (owner: serving-runtime, due: 2026-09-15)
- Expand paging policy to include CS on Severity 1 within first 10m (owner: platform oncall lead, due: 2026-08-01)
- Create a fault-injection job for batching-layer to exercise queueing limits weekly (owner: platform test, due: 2026-09-01)

What worked
- Grafana-only dashboards with linked runbooks reduced triage time by ~30% in incidents where runbooks were up-to-date.
- Automated fallback reduced outage duration in model-proxy incidents.

What needs improvement
- Observability gaps for cold-start memory usage per model. Action: add model-level memory histograms.

7. Roadmap (next three quarters)
--------------------------------
Q3 2026
- Deliver model variant canary automation (serving-runtime)
- Migrate telemetry ingestion to consumer autoscaling (observability)
- Add unified incident timeline tool and incident publisher

Q4 2026
- Release platform SLO-dashboard templates for customer-facing SLAs
- Implement per-tenant capacity dashboards and cost allocation pipeline

Q1 2027
- GA private deployment metrics collection for on-prem customers
- Integrate rollout policies into console for A/B deploys and automatic fallback

8. Team Wiki and resources
--------------------------
Canonical links and useful repos:
- Team wiki (onboarding, pager schedules): /wiki/platform-team
- Ops templates repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/platform-ops-templates.git
- Incident template: /ops/templates/incident-template.md
- SLO/SLA definitions: /confluence/product-docs/slo-and-sla-definitions

Contribution and maintenance guidance
- Editors: Platform leads may update this doc. Major edits require 1 reviewer from SRE and 1 reviewer from Serving Runtime.
- Review cadence: Quarterly (align with roadmap updates).
- If you change alert thresholds or SLOs, run the alert in staging for two weeks before updating production.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets
----------------------------
- Check current queue depth: infra-cli batching status --service batching-layer --env prod
- Toggle fallback model: infra router set-fallback --model model-xyz --variant quant-8bit-small
- Scale model-proxy: kubectl -n serving scale deployment/model-proxy --replicas=6
- View incident template: gh repo clone redwood-inference/platform-ops-templates && cat ops/templates/incident-template.md

If anything in this doc is out of date or a link is broken, open a quick PR and ping @platform-docs for a review.
